source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set Time sync with NTP server
2. Change NTP server date and time
3. Check UBB IP is available after flashed BMC Firmware

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. System date and time will change and match the NTP server date and time.
2. System date and time will follow NTP server date and time if NTP server changes.
3. Checking there is no BMC network setting change and system can still ping to Virtual nic.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl + BMC creds + reachable NTP server address
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: echo "BEFORE"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol | jq .NTP; NEW_NTP="${NTP_SERVER:?operator must set a reachable NTP server (host or IP) for the BMC}"; echo "PATCH -> NTPServers=[$NEW_NTP]"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"NTP":{"NTPServers":["$NEW_NTP"],"ProtocolEnabled":true}}' https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n"; echo "AFTER"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol | jq .NTP; echo "--- DateTime read-back ---"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/DateTime | jq .DateTime
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: BEFORE/AFTER of /redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol .NTP + DateTime read-back; user confirms NTP applied + time tracks. Agent runs on agent host per R5. Path per 11/12.RestAPI.
deepseek_columns.risk: STATE-CHANGING: patches BMC NTPServers; use reachable NTP + verify. Approval required (R6); keep PARTIAL.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL covers only an assumed Redfish NTP update and immediate readback. It uses insecure TLS and visible credentials, single-quotes a JSON payload so `$NEW_NTP` is sent literally, assumes a DateTime subresource, supplies no synchronization proof/rollback, and omits the firmware, UBB-IP and Virtual-NIC scope.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED recognizes state change, trusted transport, maintenance approval, tolerance, controlled stimulus, rollback and network evidence, but leaves the materially conflicting NTP versus post-flash network lifecycle under readiness rather than resolving the core scope.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 837/2291 preserves PARTIAL and defers command validation; it does not address the non-expanding JSON, Redfish resource discovery, destructive firmware implication or UBB/Virtual-NIC identity mismatch.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-1000 draft was inspected only as history. It correctly classified BLOCKED and separated NTP tracking from firmware/network persistence; this review independently confirms and expands that judgment.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 says missing Project inputs alone are readiness pending, but permits BLOCKED when target and core operation semantics are irreconcilable; ED-35 forbids inventing an unapproved Redfish action; ED-38 requires explicit state-change approval, recovery, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: The preserved row appears to require BMC NTP configuration and response to an NTP-source time change, while also requiring BMC-network or Virtual-NIC persistence after a BMC firmware flash; the Master does not define whether these are one lifecycle, two checkpoints or copied unrelated content.
original_method: Set BMC NTP, change an NTP server's date/time and observe tracking, then apparently flash BMC firmware and verify an undefined UBB-IP/Virtual-NIC path and unchanged BMC network settings.
manual_activity: An engineer must first decide whether the row is an NTP-only tracking test, a post-BMC-flash network-persistence test, or two separately governed checkpoints, and define BMC clock, UBB and Virtual-NIC identities. Only then may approved automation prepare an NTP workflow and, if explicitly retained, a separate firmware-update workflow.
required_inputs: Canonical scope/split and mapping of each Procedure step to each Criterion without modifying Master source
Definition of `System date and time`: BMC manager clock, host clock or both; timezone/UTC semantics, leap/step policy, tolerance, convergence window and authoritative synchronization status
Approved isolated NTP source, safe time-change stimulus, affected-client inventory, return-to-baseline plan and evidence timestamps
Exact UBB-IP and Virtual-NIC components, interface/MAC/IP/route and allowed reachability observer, plus meaning of `no BMC network setting change`
Whether a BMC firmware flash is mandatory; if yes, image identity/signature, source and target versions, update tool/API, host power state, activation/reset, success criteria and recovery
Target BMC identity, discovered vendor Redfish schema/resources/writability/ETag requirements, trusted TLS, protected credentials, maintenance window, independent OOB path and baseline restore values
Pinned reviewed internal Script commit/hash if the Script is used
safety_requirements: Do not execute this row while its NTP versus firmware/network scope and UBB/Virtual-NIC target mapping remain unresolved; an NTP-only result cannot cover post-flash persistence, and a firmware flash cannot be inferred from the title.
Do not flash BMC firmware, reset/activate the controller or alter network configuration without a separately approved image/tool/power/recovery contract.
Do not change a shared production NTP server's clock. Use an approved isolated source/stimulus and identify all clients that could be affected.
Before NTP mutation, preserve BMC identity, complete NTP/time/timezone/network state, synchronization status, logs, ETags and rollback values; never clear dmesg, syslog or SEL.
Discover the actual Manager and ManagerNetworkProtocol resources and schema from the target. Do not assume `/Managers/bmc`, a `/DateTime` child resource or writability solely from a generic example.
Do not use `curl -k`, visible basic-auth credentials or the DeepSeek payload: its single-quoted JSON sends literal `$NEW_NTP` and can misconfigure the BMC.

Do not treat HTTP success, configuration readback or one immediate timestamp as proof of NTP synchronization or tracking. Require approved status/offset samples across the convergence and stimulus windows.

Do not let a clock step silently invalidate TLS, sessions, certificates, authentication, audit correlation or scheduled tasks; stop at the approved abort threshold and use the independent recovery route.
Do not automatically retry any write, flash or activation. Preserve first-failure state and require renewed engineer direction.
agent_execution_scope: Before a scope decision, only collect source evidence and propose two non-executing plans: NTP configuration/tracking and post-flash network persistence; do not mutate BMC/NTP/network/firmware state.

After an NTP-only approval, discover the target schema, capture baseline, present the exact structured payload and rollback, wait for explicit approval, perform one write, verify persisted configuration plus authoritative sync/offset over time, apply only the approved isolated stimulus, verify tracking and restore as directed.

If firmware/network persistence is separately approved, use its own signed image, update/activation/power/recovery contract and compare exact BMC/UBB/Virtual-NIC identities and settings before/after; do not let NTP evidence substitute.
Report checkpoint facts and deviations, preserve raw evidence and stop on ambiguity or safety threshold; never issue the engineer's DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve or split the NTP and post-flash network scopes and define the authoritative clock, UBB-IP, Virtual-NIC and BMC-network semantics.
Approve isolated NTP stimulus/tolerance/convergence/rollback and, only if intended, the complete firmware image/tool/activation/recovery contract.
Approve exact discovered Redfish payload/resources and maintenance window, then review each independent checkpoint and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It is not execution-ready. The NTP read/write/readback concept covers only part of the row; `-k` and command-line credentials are unsafe, `$NEW_NTP` does not expand inside the single-quoted JSON, the manager and DateTime paths are assumed, synchronization is not demonstrated, and no firmware/UBB/Virtual-NIC checkpoint exists.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No final command may be proposed until the owner resolves the scope. For an approved NTP checkpoint, discover the target ManagerNetworkProtocol schema/resource and ETag, generate JSON structurally, use trusted TLS/protected secrets, perform one approved write and gather longitudinal sync evidence with rollback. A firmware checkpoint requires a separate plan.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All three source Procedure steps and Criteria, internal Script URL and 10/5-minute estimates remain preserved as source facts, including their unresolved mismatch.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split into checkpoint A: trusted BMC NTP configuration, convergence and isolated source-change tracking with rollback; and checkpoint B only if intended: separately authorized BMC firmware update followed by exact BMC-network and UBB/Virtual-NIC persistence comparison.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Engineer-aligned BMC manager clock, NTP implementation, update architecture and named network interfaces.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, Redfish service/schema, NTP server and firmware-update tool/image versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Target service's discovered Redfish schema and Project/vendor NTP, UBB/Virtual-NIC and BMC firmware-update specifications; DMTF ManagerNetworkProtocol defines NTP settings but not this platform's UBB or update lifecycle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the mixed lifecycles explicit and prevents an unapproved flash or unrelated NTP shortcut while retaining every Master requirement for decision.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: NTP config readback does not prove synchronization/tracking; NTP tracking does not prove network persistence; ordinary reachability does not prove unchanged settings; post-flash persistence is untested unless the separately approved update actually occurs.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner scope decision, clock/network identity maps, safe stimuli, schema, security, rollback and any complete update contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Time manipulation can break audit/authentication; NTP misconfiguration can strand clock sync; firmware update can render BMC unavailable; undefined interface mapping can yield false evidence.

project_override_considerations: A Project may approve an NTP-only case and place firmware/network persistence in a separate plan, or require both as distinct checkpoints. Record the preserved original wording, actual scope/method, reason, engineer approval and unexecuted coverage; neither checkpoint may claim the other.
expected_evidence: Signed engineer scope/split decision mapping Procedure and Criteria to independent checkpoints
BMC identity, Redfish service/schema/resource/ETag discovery, trusted client/session record and protected request metadata

NTP pre-state, exact structured update, persisted server list/enabled state, authoritative synchronization status, offset/time samples across convergence and approved source-change stimulus, and rollback/final state
Exact BMC-network, UBB-IP and Virtual-NIC identity/MAC/IP/route/link/reachability baseline and comparison from an independent observer
If firmware is retained: signed image hash, source/target version, approved tool/API, power state, update/activation/reset result, BMC recovery and post-flash network-persistence evidence
Preserved timestamped logs with clock-discontinuity annotation, no deletion, Script revision/review if used and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Test Set define an NTP-server test; Procedure steps 1-2 and Criteria 1-2 concern time synchronization. Procedure step 3 unexpectedly requires checking UBB IP after BMC firmware flashing, while Criteria 3 instead names unchanged BMC network settings and Virtual-NIC ping without defining UBB-to-Virtual-NIC equivalence or the update lifecycle. The clock subject is also called only `System`. These are materially different targets and operations.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is not blocked merely because Project values are absent. It is blocked because the preserved source combines ordinary NTP mutation/tracking with an undefined, potentially destructive BMC firmware-update and different network targets; choosing, omitting or combining those core operations by inference would change coverage and safety. An engineer scope/split decision is required.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its unsafe malformed NTP-only shortcut and restores the omitted firmware/UBB/Virtual-NIC coverage for decision.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains trusted transport, maintenance approval, tolerance, stimulus, rollback and network safeguards but changes PACKAGE to BLOCKED because the core lifecycle and target semantics—not merely execution inputs—conflict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces deferred runtime checking with explicit source-conflict and non-execution boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms its BLOCKED/source-conflict direction and adds exact Redfish discovery, malformed-payload, clock-subject and evidence requirements.

review_improvement: Prevents a malformed Redfish PATCH and immediate timestamp from falsely covering NTP tracking, and prevents an unapproved BMC flash or undefined Virtual-NIC ping from being hidden inside a time-sync test.
independent_technical_reasoning: DMTF ManagerNetworkProtocol supports an NTP object with user-supplied NTP servers, but the live service must expose its own Manager ID, schema/version and write semantics. Even a correct NTP update cannot demonstrate criteria about post-firmware network persistence. Because the Master joins distinct state machines—time synchronization and firmware/update/network recovery—and fails to identify the clock and network target, execution cannot be made safe or semantically complete through Project parameters alone.
